reason:
The facts are correct, but the severity is too high. I read the code and did not re-run the reviewer's probe.

What the code shows:
- Kernel.appendStep (apps/server/src/modules/session/kernel.ts:177-182) calls this.addSpend when detail.cost.dollars > 0.
- Kernel.addSpend (kernel.ts:239) has no link to a step. A worker that calls both charges the task and the ledger twice, and nothing throws. The reviewer's probe result (ownCost 0.02) matches this code.
- The branch does not touch docs/ARCHITECTURE.md. Lines 561 and 718 still show report.addSpend(task, $0.01, "search") as the way a search spends. Lines 385 and 604 show appendStep(taskId, step), which was already wrong on origin/main: main had (taskId, kind, text).

Why this is a nit and not should-fix:
- The diagrams are stale but still correct. addSpend exists, works, and charges once. A double charge needs an author who also fills detail.cost.
- detail.cost is documented in one place: the appendStep docstring at apps/server/src/core/domain/worker.ts:19-26. That docstring says "do not call addSpend for it as well".
- The addSpend docstring says "for a spend that is not a step's". An author who learns about detail.cost reads the prohibition in the same paragraph.
- No steering worker exists yet. demoWorker is the only caller, and it follows the rule. So no user pays double today. The risk is a future author, and a docstring on the method that author must call covers it.

Two cheap follow-ups:
- Replace the two diagram lines with appendStep(tool, {cost}).
- A guard against the double charge is a design choice, not a defect in this branch.
